$comment: The WAKE frame corpus, protocol version 4. Computed by hand from the WakeFrame production in ../wire.cddl rather than by either implementation's encoder, because vectors generated by a side under test prove nothing and there was no second codec to generate them from when this frame was specified. The relay checks itself against these bytes and so does the client; the first of them to grow a generator must reproduce this file byte for byte, exactly as scripts/call-vectors.sh does for call-frames.json. `fields` writes each frame out in its own field order so the hex is checkable by hand. `hex` and `encoded` are the same string under both names, and `name`/`id` and `reason`/`note` are the same pair, so a reader written against this file and one written against call-frames.json both work.
note: Generated from specs/backend/contracts/wire/wire.cddl. Deterministic CBOR, definite length, shortest-form integers, no tags and no floats. Registered in manifest.json, which carries the relay-state vectors for the four push error codes that no byte string can express.

vectors.name: wake-register-message-only
vectors.reason: Form 1, the canonical registration: a 16 byte handle, the message bit alone, and an expiry the relay will forget the row at. The frame carries no device identifier because the relay learns the principal from the authenticated session rather than from a field. The expiry is the year 2100 in every accepting vector here, which is not a realistic registration and is not meant to be: an elapsed expires_at is a refusal, so a corpus with a plausible date in it is a corpus that starts failing on a Tuesday.
vectors.note: Form 1, the canonical registration: a 16 byte handle, the message bit alone, and an expiry the relay will forget the row at. The frame carries no device identifier because the relay learns the principal from the authenticated session rather than from a field. The expiry is the year 2100 in every accepting vector here, which is not a realistic registration and is not meant to be: an elapsed expires_at is a refusal, so a corpus with a plausible date in it is a corpus that starts failing on a Tuesday.

vectors.name: wake-register-call-only
vectors.reason: The call bit alone. A device that wants to be rung and not otherwise disturbed is the one registration shape that has to work on a locked phone, and the relay masks every other category out rather than sending and letting the client ignore it.
vectors.note: The call bit alone. A device that wants to be rung and not otherwise disturbed is the one registration shape that has to work on a locked phone, and the relay masks every other category out rather than sending and letting the client ignore it.

vectors.name: wake-register-handshake-only
vectors.reason: The handshake bit alone, which is the top defined bit. Present so the boundary between the last defined bit and the first undefined one is covered from both sides.
vectors.note: The handshake bit alone, which is the top defined bit. Present so the boundary between the last defined bit and the first undefined one is covered from both sides.

vectors.name: wake-register-all-three
vectors.reason: Every defined bit set, which is the ordinary shape of a phone that wants messages, calls and handshakes. 7 is the largest legal mask and 8 is the first illegal one.
vectors.note: Every defined bit set, which is the ordinary shape of a phone that wants messages, calls and handshakes. 7 is the largest legal mask and 8 is the first illegal one.

vectors.name: wake-register-expires-at-width-ceiling
vectors.reason: expires_at at the ceiling of its width. CBOR encodes 2^64-1 in nine bytes and both sides must read it as a number rather than saturating it. The relay refuses an expiry already in the past and has nothing to say about one absurdly far in the future, because the GC pass is what collects the row and a ringer that mints a century is a ringer nobody has to defend against.
vectors.note: expires_at at the ceiling of its width. CBOR encodes 2^64-1 in nine bytes and both sides must read it as a number rather than saturating it. The relay refuses an expiry already in the past and has nothing to say about one absurdly far in the future, because the GC pass is what collects the row and a ringer that mints a century is a ringer nobody has to defend against.

vectors.name: wake-registered
vectors.reason: Form 2, the relay's answer to a registration: the one expiry the relay will actually honour, which is the client's own value and is echoed rather than assumed so a client never has to guess when its registration lapses.
vectors.note: Form 2, the relay's answer to a registration: the one expiry the relay will actually honour, which is the client's own value and is echoed rather than assumed so a client never has to guess when its registration lapses.

vectors.name: wake-clear
vectors.reason: Form 3. No fields at all: the row is keyed on the workspace and the authenticated principal, so there is nothing for the client to name and nothing it could name that the relay would trust.
vectors.note: Form 3. No fields at all: the row is keyed on the workspace and the authenticated principal, so there is nothing for the client to name and nothing it could name that the relay would trust.

vectors.name: wake-cleared
vectors.reason: Form 4. Answered identically whether a row existed or not, because a distinguishable answer would make this frame an oracle for whether a principal holds a registration.
vectors.note: Form 4. Answered identically whether a row existed or not, because a distinguishable answer would make this frame an oracle for whether a principal holds a registration.

vectors.name: wake-query
vectors.reason: Form 5. The frame that makes a self-hosted deployment work with a shipped client: the device does not know which ringer to register with and must not guess, because guessing ours would register a self-hoster's users with a ringer their operator did not choose.
vectors.note: Form 5. The frame that makes a self-hosted deployment work with a shipped client: the device does not know which ringer to register with and must not guess, because guessing ours would register a self-hoster's users with a ringer their operator did not choose.

vectors.name: wake-capability-on
vectors.reason: Form 6 with push configured. The relay states the ringer rather than the client assuming one. Asked over this frame and never at CONNECT_ACK time, because adding a field to CONNECT_ACK is the one thing a version negotiation must not require.
vectors.note: Form 6 with push configured. The relay states the ringer rather than the client assuming one. Asked over this frame and never at CONNECT_ACK time, because adding a field to CONNECT_ACK is the one thing a version negotiation must not require.

vectors.name: wake-capability-off
vectors.reason: Form 6 with push off, which is the default and a supported deployment rather than a degraded one. The empty url is legal and load bearing: a client reading enabled false holds no registration and raises no expectation of push, so there is nothing for a url to mean.
vectors.note: Form 6 with push off, which is the default and a supported deployment rather than a degraded one. The empty url is legal and load bearing: a client reading enabled false holds no registration and raises no expectation of push, so there is nothing for a url to mean.

vectors.name: wake-capability-url-at-ceiling
vectors.reason: A register_url of exactly 512 bytes. The boundary is inclusive, as it is for every other ceiling in this protocol: a bound a client cannot reach is a bound it cannot plan against. The vector one byte over is below.
vectors.note: A register_url of exactly 512 bytes. The boundary is inclusive, as it is for every other ceiling in this protocol: a bound a client cannot reach is a bound it cannot plan against. The vector one byte over is below.

vectors.name: wake-reject-handle-fifteen-bytes
vectors.reason: A 15 byte handle. reject/push_handle_malformed, and a reject rather than a denial because a wrong-length handle is permanently wrong as sent and resending it would be wrong in the same way.
vectors.note: A 15 byte handle. reject/push_handle_malformed, and a reject rather than a denial because a wrong-length handle is permanently wrong as sent and resending it would be wrong in the same way.

vectors.name: wake-reject-handle-seventeen-bytes
vectors.reason: A 17 byte handle. The other side of the same boundary, present because a length check written as a minimum passes this and a length check written as a maximum passes the vector above it.
vectors.note: A 17 byte handle. The other side of the same boundary, present because a length check written as a minimum passes this and a length check written as a maximum passes the vector above it.

vectors.name: wake-reject-categories-zero
vectors.reason: An empty bitmask. At least one bit must be set: a registration that admits no category is a row that can never produce a wake, and storing one would leave a device believing it had registered for something.
vectors.note: An empty bitmask. At least one bit must be set: a registration that admits no category is a row that can never produce a wake, and storing one would leave a device believing it had registered for something.

vectors.name: wake-reject-categories-undefined-bit
vectors.reason: Bit 8 set alongside the message bit. The category set is closed at three values and an undefined bit is refused rather than masked away, so a future client cannot widen what a wake means without a version bump.
vectors.note: Bit 8 set alongside the message bit. The category set is closed at three values and an undefined bit is refused rather than masked away, so a future client cannot widen what a wake means without a version bump.

vectors.name: wake-reject-categories-only-undefined-bit
vectors.reason: Bit 8 alone. Refused by the undefined-bit rule and not by the empty-mask rule, and the pair matters: an implementation that only checked for zero would accept this and hold a registration admitting nothing it can name.
vectors.note: Bit 8 alone. Refused by the undefined-bit rule and not by the empty-mask rule, and the pair matters: an implementation that only checked for zero would accept this and hold a registration admitting nothing it can name.

vectors.name: wake-reject-expires-at-not-a-uint
vectors.reason: expires_at as a text string carrying the same digits. reject/malformed_header rather than the push code, because the field is not of its declared type and the codec refuses it before the push path is reached, exactly as it refuses a wrong-length content hash.
vectors.note: expires_at as a text string carrying the same digits. reject/malformed_header rather than the push code, because the field is not of its declared type and the codec refuses it before the push path is reached, exactly as it refuses a wrong-length content hash.

vectors.name: wake-reject-expires-at-already-past
vectors.reason: A well-formed expiry that has already elapsed. Refused rather than stored and immediately collected, because a row the GC pass would remove on its next sweep is a registration the device would spend a week believing in.
vectors.note: A well-formed expiry that has already elapsed. Refused rather than stored and immediately collected, because a row the GC pass would remove on its next sweep is a registration the device would spend a week believing in.

vectors.name: wake-reject-register-url-not-https
vectors.reason: A plaintext register_url. Refused by the client, which is the direction this form travels: a device that registered over http would hand its APNs token to whatever answered, and the whole design is built on the token reaching exactly one party.
vectors.note: A plaintext register_url. Refused by the client, which is the direction this form travels: a device that registered over http would hand its APNs token to whatever answered, and the whole design is built on the token reaching exactly one party.

vectors.name: wake-reject-register-url-513-bytes
vectors.reason: One byte past the 512 byte ceiling. Refused on the declared length, so the vector immediately above it and this one differ by exactly the byte the check is about.
vectors.note: One byte past the 512 byte ceiling. Refused on the declared length, so the vector immediately above it and this one differ by exactly the byte the check is about.

vectors.name: wake-reject-indefinite-length-handle
vectors.reason: The handle as an indefinite-length byte string whose single chunk is the same 16 bytes. Deterministic CBOR is a validation rule and not a convention, so this is refused even though it decodes to a handle the relay would otherwise have stored.
vectors.note: The handle as an indefinite-length byte string whose single chunk is the same 16 bytes. Deterministic CBOR is a validation rule and not a convention, so this is refused even though it decodes to a handle the relay would otherwise have stored.

vectors.name: wake-reject-nonshortest-categories
vectors.reason: categories 1 encoded as a two-byte uint. Refused for the reason every other non-shortest integer in this protocol is: an encoder artifact must not be able to produce two byte strings that mean one frame.
vectors.note: categories 1 encoded as a two-byte uint. Refused for the reason every other non-shortest integer in this protocol is: an encoder artifact must not be able to produce two byte strings that mean one frame.

vectors.name: wake-reject-map-where-an-array-is-required
vectors.reason: A Clear whose wake-fields is an empty map rather than an empty array. The grammar says array everywhere and the two encode differently, so a decoder loose enough to take either is a decoder two implementations can disagree inside.
vectors.note: A Clear whose wake-fields is an empty map rather than an empty array. The grammar says array everywhere and the two encode differently, so a decoder loose enough to take either is a decoder two implementations can disagree inside.

vectors.name: wake-reject-trailing-byte
vectors.reason: A complete Query followed by one extra byte. A frame is exactly one CBOR item and nothing after it, so trailing data is refused rather than ignored: a decoder that stops at the end of the item leaves an attacker a byte of channel nobody is validating.
vectors.note: A complete Query followed by one extra byte. A frame is exactly one CBOR item and nothing after it, so trailing data is refused rather than ignored: a decoder that stops at the end of the item leaves an attacker a byte of channel nobody is validating.

vectors.name: wake-reject-over-the-frame-ceiling
vectors.reason: 1036 bytes, past the 1 KiB WAKE ceiling. Refused on the declared frame length before the body is decoded, so the fourth element is never reached and the refusal names the frame ceiling rather than the arity it would otherwise have complained about.
vectors.note: 1036 bytes, past the 1 KiB WAKE ceiling. Refused on the declared frame length before the body is decoded, so the fourth element is never reached and the refusal names the frame ceiling rather than the arity it would otherwise have complained about.

vectors.name: wake-reject-unknown-form
vectors.reason: Form 7. The form set is closed at six and an unrecognised value is refused rather than carried, which is the same rule the closed call-kind set has and for the same reason: routing semantics do not change without a version bump.
vectors.note: Form 7. The form set is closed at six and an unrecognised value is refused rather than carried, which is the same rule the closed call-kind set has and for the same reason: routing semantics do not change without a version bump.

vectors.name: wake-reject-register-wrong-arity
vectors.reason: A Register carrying two fields instead of three. Refused on arity rather than defaulted, because a missing expires_at defaulted to anything would be the relay choosing how long a wake capability lives.
vectors.note: A Register carrying two fields instead of three. Refused on arity rather than defaulted, because a missing expires_at defaulted to anything would be the relay choosing how long a wake capability lives.
